test_title: SSC Selection Post 2024 (Graduate Level) Official Paper (Held On: 20 Jun, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Under which Schedule of the Indian Constitution is the form of oath or affirmation for a Judge of the Supreme Court mentioned?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Third Schedule**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The form of oath or affirmation for a Judge of the Supreme Court is mentioned in the **Third Schedule** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Third Schedule also includes forms of oath or affirmation for other constitutional positions such as the President, Vice-President, Ministers, Members of Parliament, and Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.
 
• Taking an oath or affirmation is a mandatory requirement before assuming office for these constitutional positions.
 
• The oath or affirmation signifies the commitment to uphold the Constitution and discharge duties faithfully and impartially.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Third Schedule** is a part of the Constitution that provides the forms of oaths and affirmations for various constitutional offices.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• Oaths and affirmations are a crucial aspect of maintaining the integrity and accountability of individuals holding constitutional positions.
